newsitem.title: USA: American Banknote loses class action suit.
newsitem.headline: American Banknote loses class action suit.

text.p: American Banknote Corp said Monday a jury had decided against it in a class action suit filed in 1994 by stockholder Bert Vladimir.
The company said any damages paid to members of the class will be provided by an insurance policy and will not impact company operations and operating results.

The suit alleged the company made misstatements and/or omissions in 1993 concerning its predictions that it would continue to receive substantial business from the U.S. Postal Service in 1994 and beyond, said a statement by American Banknotes.
The jury, in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, found damages of $0.79 per share for purchasers of shares during the nine months of the class period, the statement said.
The company said it has asked the judge to set aside the jury decision.

The company said it intends to establish a reserve to be recorded in the fourth quarter of 1996, which after giving effect to insurance coverage is expected to result in a one-time charge of about $0.07 per share.

"There is no way to predict how many claims will be filed for damages, but whatever the amount may be, it is sure to be covered by our $10 million insurance policy," said Executive Vice President and General Counsel Harvey Kesner.
